newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Soft drinks to deaden Cadbury fizz.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Soft drinks to deaden Cadbury fizz.

text.p: Drinks and confectionery group Cadbury Schweppes Plc is set to show a respectable profit increase when it reports full year figures next Wednesday, food industry analysts said.
But worries about intense competition in the U.S. soft drinks market, where Cadbury is the third biggest player, could overshadow the results.

Investment analysts predicted on Friday pretax profits of between 585 million stg and 592 million up from 526 million the previous year. The profits exclude the 623 million stg from Cadbury's sale of its 51 percent stake in the Coca-Cola Schweppes Beverages bottling and distribution business to Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc, completed last month.
The forecasts also strip out restructuring costs of about 40 million stg, analysts said.

The deal will reduce debt and puts the company in a more comfortable financial position, raising questions about how it will invest the cash. When the deal was completed Cadbury said it would use the money to develop its branded business worldwide.

Attention will focus closely on how Cadbury's soft drinks business is performing in the United States, where some analysts fear it is being squeezed hard by Coca-Cola and PepsiCo. "The biggest area of concern is U.S. drinks business," said Michael Bourke at Panmure Gordon.

He is forecasting the U.S. beverages business will make operating profits of 279 million stg, up from 238 million. "Profits are growing comfortably, but they are losing a bit of market share," he said.

Other analysts were more relaxed about the competitive pressures on soft drinks. Richard Newbolt at Lehman Brothers downplayed the market's worries that Cadbury was stuck between Coke and Pepsi and would suffer as a result.
He was dismissive of recent speculation that Unilever might want to takeover Cadbury, using cash from its speciality chemicals sale." It's just idle speculation," he said.
The shares, which had been performing poorly, have been buoyed by the takeover talk. Panmure recommends them as a "hold".
The dividend is forecast to be around 17 pence a share up from 16 pence.
